latest.title: Wales fightback not enough as Australia edge thriller thanks to Gordon
latest.summary: Wales 26-29 Australia Wales to face Japan in ninth-place final One step at a time. Historic victories are one thing, but the boring need to back up such a win proved beyond Wales. Cardiff was rocking. A few thousand short of capacity the stadium may have been, but 66,000 rocked it as of yore. Wales’s young side could not quite respond. This was a reverse of last weekend’s win against New Zealand . In the first half, in particular, Wales’s dominance was all but total, but like the All Blacks, they just could not make it tell. Australia had the lead at the break and in a more open second half they proved just as deadly. Thus they claim their place in the fifth-place final at Twickenham, where they will face Ireland on Friday night. Wales must make do with a ninth-placed final against Japan on Saturday. Science.title: A 50-year-old theory about evolution may have been wrong all along
Science.summary: A decades-old theory suggesting that evolution protects its most important genes from mutations has been dealt a major blow. An extensive new analysis of mutations in bacteria and yeast found no evidence that essential genes mutate less frequently than other genes. Researchers say earlier studies may have been misled by harmful mutations that disappeared through natural selection before scientists could detect them.

Culture.title: SNL’s skit Sister captures the quiet agony of caregiving for women: ‘I’ve never felt seen like that’
Culture.summary: The viral satirization of the caregiving burden left to women and daughters hit home for many viewers The Saturday Night Live sketch , titled Sister quickly went viral this week for its satirization of the burden that women and daughters face to take care of aging family members. In the parody commercial, comedian John Mulaney touts the benefit of “Sister”, who he describes as “a live-in 24/7 elder care provider that is completely free, and also your sister” . “Now I don’t have to worry about dad getting the care and attention he needs because my sister will do it, and I can get back to my life, and the stuff I like to do,” Mulaney says, as the sister, played by cast member Jane Wickline, gives their father’s medication to him. The sketch, which amassed over seven million views on YouTube in less than a week since it aired, has received thousands of responses and comments about its accuracy. “This is one of the MOST wicked and spot on SNL sketches ever written,” wrote one commenter on YouTube. Another posted: “As a hospice nurse this definitely tracks. I deal 90% of the time with adult daughters, and if there is no daughter, it is the daughter in law.” “This is so real it almost gave me a stroke from rage,” added another viewer. Continue reading...
